newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire appeals for calm as fear grips capital.
newsitem.headline: Zaire appeals for calm as fear grips capital.

text.p: The military governor of Zaire's capital Kinshasa appealed for calm on Sunday following what he called widespread panic over a possible attack on the city by rebels.

"An atmosphere of panic, due essentially to the situation in the east of our country, reigns among Kinshasa's men and women," General Amela Lokima said in a special broadcast. It followed the expiry of a deadline for President Mobutu Sese Seko to quit or face all-out war from rebels who hold nearly half the country.
"The most fantastic rumours according to which the city of Kinshasa would soon fall to the armed rebellion are gaining ground," Amela said.
He called on Zaireans and foreigners living in the city to remain calm, adding: "The Security of our capital is our fundamental duty".
The television announcer said panic had gripped the districts of Kinshasa close to the airport after anti-Mobutu militants urged residents to evacuate.

Opposition militants, who have declared support for rebel leader Laurent Kabila, have called for a total shutdown of the capital on Monday as part of a campaign to force an end to Mobutu's 32-year rule.
